title: Existence of a normal finite etale extension on a smooth trait
statement: Let A be a Noetherian normal local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] of Krull dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let q:L→Spec A [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth with geometrically connected fibres [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let V be the complement of the closed point. Let n:N→L be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and etale over q⁻¹V [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose n is etale on an open W of L containing a point x over the closed point. Then there exist a finite etale p:E→L with all local rings of E normal domains, dense p⁻¹(q⁻¹V) in E, and an isomorphism N|q⁻¹V ≅ E|q⁻¹V over q⁻¹V. No normality or density hypothesis on N is imposed.

proof.text: Split on IsField A. In the field case its spectrum has one point, so hV makes V empty. Take E to be the empty open subscheme of L and p its inclusion. The inclusion is finite etale; normality and density are vacuous. Both restrictions are empty schemes, and their initial-object isomorphism has the required composition equation. This branch is fully proved in Lean.

In the nonfield case, ringKrullDim A ≤ 1 makes every nonzero prime maximal (Mathlib Ideal.IsPrime.isMaximal_of_ne_bot). Normality and Noetherianity then give IsDedekindDomain A, and IsDiscreteValuationRing.TFAE supplies the DVR structure. Apply [lem-sbc-dvr-punctured-cover-purity] to obtain p:E→L finite etale and the restriction isomorphism. The private trait_isDVR helper and the assembly are fully proved.

The composite p≫q is smooth. Its base Spec A has normal domain stalks by localization of A [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. In the private smooth_normal_stalks helper, choose affine neighborhoods in source and target, transfer base-stalk normality to prime localizations of the base chart, apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-normal-ring-normal] to the smooth chart map, and transfer the two properties from the source chart localization back to its stalk. This proves normal domain stalks of E without using the separate etale-normality theorem.

The zero prime of the nonfield local domain differs from its closed point, so hV makes V nonempty. Spec A is irreducible and V is open, hence V is dense. The smooth composite p≫q is an open map. Apply Mathlib Dense.preimage and rewrite Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage to obtain the required dense puncture of E. Assemble finiteness, etaleness, normality, density and the compatible restriction isomorphism. All of this step is proved in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_etale_extension_of_trait_neighbourhood
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsDomain A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A]
    {L N : Scheme.{u}} (q : L ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [QuasiCompact q] [QuasiSeparated q] [Smooth q] [GeometricallyConnected q]
    (V : (Spec (.of A)).Opens)
    (hV : ∀ t : Spec (.of A), t ∈ V ↔ t ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)
    (n : N ⟶ L) [IsFinite n]
    (het : Etale (n ∣_ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)))
    (W : L.Opens) (x : L) (hx : x ∈ W)
    (hqx : q x = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) (hW : Etale (n ∣_ W))
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A ≤ (1 : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ (E : Scheme.{u}) (p : E ⟶ L), IsFinite p ∧ Etale p ∧
      (∀ z : E, IsDomain (E.presheaf.stalk z) ∧
        IsIntegrallyClosed (E.presheaf.stalk z)) ∧
      Dense (↑(p ⁻¹ᵁ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)) : Set E) ∧
      ∃ e : (n ⁻¹ᵁ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)).toScheme ≅ (p ⁻¹ᵁ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)).toScheme,
        e.hom ≫ (p ∣_ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)) = n ∣_ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)
